title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident shows an impersonation attack using AI-generated deepfake videos and synthetic identity creation to commit fraud. Scammers deployed the system on social media platforms where immigrants were likely to encounter it, targeting a vulnerable population seeking legal services. The system was never designed for this purpose and operated entirely outside any legitimate deployment context, but there was no human verification by the platforms that the profiles and videos were authentic before they were distributed at scale.

The failure to catch this earlier lay with social media platforms' content moderation systems. An anti-piracy firm eventually removed thousands of fake accounts, but this happened only after the attorney discovered the scheme and hired the firm himself. Suspicious activity had been running for months before removal began. Whether platform moderation could have detected the deepfakes and fake accounts sooner is not established by these reports.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, is the victim of an elaborate AI scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and deepfake videos featuring Leal offering immigration services he never provides, including US residency assistance for $2,200 and immigration detention release services. The scams direct people through WhatsApp to contact fraudulent numbers, where they receive fake contracts and payment requests via Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

Leal first discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity began last October and dramatically escalated over the past three months. His company hired an anti-piracy firm that has removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Leal is urging immigrants to verify attorney credentials and avoid paying for legal services through phone or digital payment apps. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scam's origins.
